title: WALK fs_edit FAILS ON AN ABSOLUTE PATH UNDER /workspace/repos, WHICH EXISTS BUT IS NOT AN ALLOWED ROOT — 64 OCCURRENCES.
description: WALK fs_edit FAILS ON AN ABSOLUTE PATH UNDER /workspace/repos, WHICH EXISTS BUT IS NOT AN ALLOWED ROOT — 64 OCCURRENCES. MEASURED 2026-09-05 from dispatch 618754d7: goal-host logged 'walk rawResolve fs_edit: HTTP 500 {error: path outside workspace root: /workspace/repos/activity-api/src/routes/goal-paths.ts}'. The goal-host journal holds 64 occurrences of that message. CORRECTED ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS, replacing my first statement of this gap. The guard in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/workspace-roots.ts already handles RELATIVE paths correctly — resolveWithin resolves a relative path against each candidate root and checks containment against that same root, a fix whose in-file comment documents this exact symptom for relative inputs. The failing path here is ABSOLUTE, so resolve() leaves it at /workspace/repos/... and containment fails against allowedWorkspaceRoots, which is WORKSPACE_ROOT (/workspace/git/super-repo) plus anything in EXTRA_WORKSPACE_ROOTS. goal-host's OWN path builders are not the source: they construct /workspace/git/super-repo/<rel>, /workspace/git/vessels/<vessel>, and /vessels/<vessel>, all of which are allowed or resolvable. The offending absolute path therefore appears to be synthesized upstream (an LLM-emitted tool argument) and passed through unvalidated rather than normalised to a known root. THE COMPLICATION: /workspace/repos IS REAL and holds the file (57,660 bytes, Aug 29) — it is not a hallucinated path, it is a fourth copy. The same file exists at /workspace/git/vessels/... (57,660, Aug 29) and at /workspace/git/super-repo/repos/... (55,693, Aug 16). So simply adding /workspace/repos to EXTRA_WORKSPACE_ROOTS would make the write succeed against a copy that may not be the one the cutover reads, and the in-root super-repo copy is about two weeks stale. Deciding WHICH copy is canonical is part of this gap, not incidental to it. CONSEQUENCE: walk-based edits to repos/<vessel>/src cannot land; only feature_compose can, because it carries its own path handling. That is why a capacity-capped compose lane blocks all code change rather than merely slowing it. FALSIFIER: closed only when a walk-dispatched (not compose-dispatched) edit to a repos/<vessel>/src file completes with no 'path outside workspace root' error AND the edited file's byte size matches the copy the mitosis cutover reads. Cite the dispatch id, the resolved absolute path, and both byte sizes. A closure citing neither is fabricated.
